topics.topic: Accepted multipart port-name and file media-type syntax
questions: Which port-name and media-type syntax is accepted for bindings that can produce multipart requests, and how are quotes, backslashes, controls and non-ASCII characters handled?
Which port names are legal in multipart bindings, and how are legal non-token characters encoded in Content-Disposition parameters?
How are quotes, backslashes, control characters, non-ASCII text and other unsafe characters in multipart port names handled?
What media-type grammar is accepted for file ports, and are parameters permitted?

quotes:
Each part has exactly two
   headers: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with
   `filename="<port>"` added for a file part, and `Content-Type`, the port's
   media type for a file part and `application/json` for a value part, without
   parameters; nothing else.
judgement.why: The cited multipart construction was unchanged, and the reopening change did not make its syntax question matter.

topics.topic: Agent-name and token identity rules across configuration reloads
questions: What happens when a reloaded token list contains duplicate agent names, reuses an old name for another token, or changes the name attached to an existing token?
What happens when a live configuration reload introduces two agent tokens with the same agent_name?
Must a live token-list reload reject duplicate agent names, or may it create two indistinguishable Actor values?

quotes:
Exactly three checks apply to a re-read: the
   file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two
   tokens are equal.
judgement.why: The live-reload checks were unchanged, and the reopening change did not affect agent-name identity.

topics.topic: Complete structural schema and validation ordering for manifests
questions: What exact manifest JSON structure is accepted, including duplicate selected-instance names, wrong field types, unknown fields and required-header representation?
What complete manifest schema is accepted, and how are wrong types, duplicate JSON member names and malformed nested records classified and ordered?
What complete structural schema must a manifest record satisfy, and which ordered manifest-mismatch reason covers each malformed shape?

judgement.why: This asks for complete schemas, field types and malformed-field classification, which belong to State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Conversion, sanitization, and bounding of arbitrary response bytes in failure_detail
questions: How are arbitrary response bytes decoded and sanitized for `failure_detail`, and what unit is disclosed as its length?
How is a non-UTF-8 error body represented in failure_detail, and is the byte limit applied before or after conversion?
How is an arbitrary binary or invalid-UTF-8 error body converted into bounded failure-detail text?

quotes:
The body of
   an error response is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it
   is kept as `failure_detail`, whose class is the highest of the execution's
   class and the classes the binding declares for its outputs, under A07 rule 5.
judgement.why: The error-body excerpt rule was unchanged, and the reopening change did not create the encoding question.

topics.topic: Filesystem access permitted to sandboxed function code
questions: May function code directly enumerate, read and write the exchange directory or read arbitrary runtime files, or must all filesystem access except the runner's own input/output handling be trapped?
May function code read runtime files and create or modify files in the exchange directory, or must all filesystem access other than reading its supplied inputs fail?
May agent code itself read and write paths in the exchange directory or read runtime files, or are those paths exclusively for the trusted runner?

quotes:
Before loading the module, the in-sandbox runner replaces every clock and
   randomness entry point of the standard library (`time`, `datetime` current-time
   functions, `os.urandom`, `random` seeding, `secrets`) with one that raises, and
   installs an audit hook that raises on socket, subprocess, `ctypes` and on
   opening any path outside the exchange directory and the read-only runtime.
judgement.why: The sandbox filesystem allowance was unchanged, and the reopening change did not alter its significance.

topics.topic: HTTPS verification policy and HTTP loopback exception classification
questions: What verification policy and trust store are used for HTTPS, and exactly which URL hosts count as loopback for the HTTP exception?
What exact TLS verification policy and trust roots must the HTTP invoker use?
Which trust store, hostname-verification rules, protocol versions, certificate constraints and client behavior constitute successful TLS verification?

quotes:
TLS is verified for `https`. Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
judgement.why: The TLS and loopback policy was unchanged, and the reopening change did not make its unspecified details matter.

topics.topic: Meaning and enforcement of deterministic function execution
questions: Is deterministic output a guaranteed sandbox property, a property tested by repeated executions, or merely an expectation of agent code?
What mechanism makes deterministic output enforceable, or what outcome is required when identical executions differ?
Does deterministic admission mean only a fixed checking algorithm, or must the same implementation and case always produce the same execution outcome and output?

quotes: 6. The same implementation on the same input yields the same output digest twice.
judgement.why: The deterministic-execution requirement was unchanged, and the reopening change did not affect how it is enforced.

topics.topic: Outcome when an HTTP response body fails after final status and headers
questions: Once a final status line and headers are received, which transport failures while reading the body override the status-based outcome?
If the status and headers are valid but the error-response body is incomplete, is the outcome determined by the status or treated as no valid final response?
Which table row wins when a final status is received but its body is incomplete or times out?

quotes:
"Nothing could be sent" holds only when the failure happened before the
   kernel wrote the first byte of the request; any failure after that, before a
   status line arrived, is "may have been sent".
judgement.why: The transport boundary around receipt of a status line was unchanged, and the reopening change did not affect incomplete response bodies.

topics.topic: Permitted service base URLs and exact URL and Host construction
questions: Which exact `api_base_url` forms are permitted, and how are its path, query and fragment components combined with the declared operation path?
Which base URL components are allowed, and what exact URL and Host header result from each accepted representation?
May `api_base_url` contain a path, query, fragment, user information, Unicode host, or multiple trailing slashes, and exactly how are those cases joined and represented in the Host header?

quotes:
The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host;
judgement.why: The base-URL joining rule was unchanged, and the reopening change did not make additional URL forms matter.

topics.topic: Actor provenance recorded for executions, verdicts, and attempts
questions: How does every execution, verdict and attempt identify the owner, named agent or kernel action that caused it?
How must each execution and attempt record identify whether it resulted from an owner request, an agent request, admission, or startup recovery?

quotes:
The owner's actions,
each agent's and the kernel's own are distinguishable in every record.
judgement.why: The actor-provenance requirement was unchanged, and the added attempt fields did not make the preexisting provenance question matter.

topics.topic: Allowed encoding and grammar of credential and HTTP header values
questions: What byte or character grammar must a resolved credential value satisfy before it is placed in an HTTP header?
What byte encoding is used for non-ASCII HTTP header values and credential values, or must such values be refused?

judgement.why: This asks for the accepted encoding and grammar of header values, which is format closure for State 6 or later.

topics.topic: Canonical ordering of equal-key flow edges and constants
questions: How are equal-key edges and constants ordered for canonical hashing and for selecting the first proof failure?
What total tie-break order applies to distinct edges with identical endpoints but different guards?
How are equal-destination constants ordered for identity hashing and for selecting the first proof failure?

quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
judgement.why: The canonical sorting keys were unchanged, and the reopening change did not create the equal-key case.

topics.topic: Data-directory creation, ownership, and permission requirements
questions: What exact ownership and permission checks apply to the data directory and each contained file, and what happens when the configured directory does not exist?
What exact filesystem ownership and permission conditions make the data directory and its contents private?

quotes:
The directory and everything in it
   are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
judgement.why: The data-directory privacy requirement was unchanged, and the reopening change did not affect its filesystem details.

topics.topic: Preventing credentials from appearing in untrusted failure data
questions: How is the no-credential-in-failure-detail invariant enforced when an untrusted service response can contain that credential verbatim or encoded?
Does the prohibition concern only credential values inserted by the kernel, or must the kernel detect and suppress the same bytes when an untrusted caller or service returns them?

quotes:
It never enters the store, a record, a trace, a preview, a
   failure detail, a log line, a process argument or a response.
judgement.why: The credential non-disclosure invariant was unchanged, and the reopening change did not create the service-echo problem.

topics.topic: Retry scope and eligibility after a not_applied outcome
questions: What counts as repeating an effect: only another attempt of the same run element, or any later send with the same binding, request or idempotency key across runs; and can a direct 4xx attempt ever be resent?
Can a direct 4xx `not_applied` attempt be retried in the same run, and if so what action causes the fresh approval and new attempt?

quotes:
A node is failed when its record's status is `contract_violation`,
   `sandbox_violation`, `timeout`, `resource_exhausted`, `crashed`,
   `operation_refused` or `operation_failed`; `service_unreachable` and
   `outcome_unknown` are waits, not failures, and their dependants wait, until
   the owner's resolution makes the element count as succeeded or failed
   (A11 rule 3).

When nothing can
   execute and nothing waits, the run ends: `succeeded` when every node concluded
   succeeded or `skipped_by_guard`; otherwise `failed`.

Two runs on equal inputs
   are two runs; protection against a repeated effect is the owner's approval and
   the idempotency key, never a deduplication of runs.
judgement.why: A direct 4xx makes the element fail and cannot be retried in that run, while a later run is distinct and is governed by its normal authority and idempotency key.

topics.topic: Scope of prohibited clock, timing, and randomness APIs
questions: Does the prohibition cover deterministic pseudorandom generators and every API exposing time or timing, including APIs absent from A03's closed trap list?
Is the closed trap list authoritative even though it leaves clock sources available, or must all observable clock sources be blocked?

quotes:
`random.Random(seed)`
   with an explicit seed stays usable. The list is closed for the release; an
   entry point found missing is added by a new release.
judgement.why: The seeded-random exception and closed trap list were unchanged, and the reopening change did not affect their scope.

topics.topic: Accepted idempotency declarations for read operations
questions: For a read operation, are missing, malformed or non-text idempotency_key declarations accepted, and if accepted what value is stored in idempotency_key_fields?

topics.topic: Accepted values for required purpose fields
questions: What exact values satisfy the required `purpose` check?

topics.topic: Activation using a cached admission verdict
questions: Can resubmitting an implementation with a cached admitted verdict activate it without creating a new verdict?

topics.topic: Allowed credential references and secret-file security checks
questions: What forms of credential reference are allowed, and what filesystem security checks apply before reading the secret value?

topics.topic: Authority for autonomous startup recovery advancement
questions: Is automatic startup advancement an additional authorized autonomous kernel action, despite State 0's exhaustive statement?

topics.topic: Completeness and uniqueness requirements for authored expected outputs
questions: When expected_outputs is present, must it contain exactly one value for every output port, and are unknown or duplicate output names refused?

topics.topic: Crash consistency between published files and database records
questions: After a crash or database failure between publishing a file and committing its record, must the completed unreferenced file be removed, retained and reused, or considered outside the atomic-change guarantee?

topics.topic: Crash-safe spool retention and deletion during release and cleanup
questions: After a crash during release or terminal-run cleanup, how is it guaranteed that an unreleased failed run has its files and that a released run does not retain them?

topics.topic: Detection of sandbox resource-limit violations caught by user code
questions: What observable event constitutes a memory, process-count or scratch limit hit, especially when user code catches the resulting error and returns valid output?

topics.topic: Effect of dependency upgrades on active implementations and cached verdicts
questions: After an upgrade changes Python or another execution dependency, may an old activation continue and may its cached verdict be reused without re-admission?

topics.topic: Events defining NodeExecution start and end timestamps
questions: What events define `started_at` and `ended_at` for function calls, pre-send failures, approval refusals, service attempts, skips and upstream failures?

topics.topic: Exact JSON request bytes and Content-Type
questions: What exact bytes and Content-Type are used for a non-multipart JSON request body?

topics.topic: Failure and record retention for oversized mapped aggregate outputs
questions: If individually successful mapped elements form an aggregate JSON array larger than stored_value_bytes_max, which NodeExecution records the failure, what happens to already written successful element records, and are any aggregate outputs retained?

topics.topic: Handling and limiting sandbox stdout and stderr
questions: Are stdout and stderr discarded, captured within a limit, or counted against a resource bound, and what outcome results from excessive output?

topics.topic: Information class of an empty mapped-operation output
questions: What class does an empty output list from a mapped operation node receive when the mapped input and binding output classes differ?

topics.topic: Information-class propagation through operation nodes
questions: May an operation receiving personal_data or business_confidential input produce an output declared at a lower class, or must its effective output class be at least the highest input class?

topics.topic: Invocable GET and DELETE input cardinality and schema combinations
questions: Which combinations of `cardinality` and schema type are invocable as query parameters?

topics.topic: Meaning and enforcement of schemas on file ports
questions: What does a JSON Schema on a file port describe, and is anything about a file validated against it beyond canonical equality between connected ports?

topics.topic: Multipart boundary generation and collision handling
questions: How is the multipart boundary generated, and what happens if it occurs in a part's bytes?

topics.topic: Multiplicity and syntax requirements for file-response Content-Type
questions: Must a successful file response contain exactly one syntactically valid Content-Type field value?

topics.topic: Persistence and reuse of records after interrupted trials or admission
questions: After an interrupted try or admission, which implementation, TrialExecution and AdmissionVerdict records remain, and does a later submission reuse or rerun partial work?

topics.topic: Pinned dependency versions defining release v1
questions: Which exact dependency versions constitute release v1 and are required for startup or build acceptance?

topics.topic: ProofResult identity for failures involving constants or ports
questions: What object does ProofResult identify when the failing item is a constant or a port rather than an edge or node?

topics.topic: Reading and handling unavailable manifest revisions
questions: How does the kernel read `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` at `manifest_revision`, and is an unavailable revision a startup failure or a per-proposal/per-send manifest failure?

topics.topic: Required cardinality of path-placeholder inputs
questions: Must every path-placeholder input port have cardinality one, or may a binding be accepted that can only fail at send time?

topics.topic: Rollback validation when the requested target is the current implementation
questions: If the current implementation lacks a verdict over a newly grown corpus, does a rollback request naming that same current implementation return the activation or refuse it?

topics.topic: Startup check and recovery ordering, precedence, and allowed mutations
questions: In what order are startup checks and recovery performed, which failure is reported when several apply, and which filesystem or run mutations may occur before all startup checks pass?

topics.topic: Supported-schema validation and failure ordering for binding ports
questions: Must every proposed binding port schema be in the supported schema subset, and where does that check occur in A08's failure order?

topics.topic: Validation and rejection ordering for standing grants targeting function nodes
questions: Is a request to grant a function node refused, and at which check relative to active-version and duplicate-grant checks?

topics.topic: Validation and storage semantics for many-cardinality values
questions: For constants, authored and captured trial cases, expected outputs, service outputs and stored-value identities, is a `many` value validated as one array against the port schema or as a list whose elements each satisfy the port schema, and which schema is stored in its `StoredValue`?

topics.topic: Validity and reserved use of flow, slot, node, and port identifiers
questions: May `flow_id`, `slot_id`, `node_id` and port names be empty, and may a real node use the empty string reserved for flow endpoints?

topics.topic: Whether multipart serialization changes invalidate request approval
questions: Does a changed multipart boundary or resulting Content-Length make a different approved request?

topics.topic: Which implementations are eligible rollback targets
questions: Is rollback allowed to select any non-current implementation admitted over the current corpus, only an implementation submitted before the current implementation, or only one that appeared in an earlier activation?
